The app stays free and open source; a coffee keeps releases quick

Life Dashboard Companion is a self-hosting tool. It reads health and screen time data on this phone and sends it only to servers you set up yourself. The developer never receives, stores or sees any of your data.

Health Connect records, only for the types you switch on and only after you grant the permission. App usage statistics for Screen Time, through usage access. With the history permission, records older than 30 days for a one-off backfill. The camera is used only by the pairing scanner, while that screen is open: frames are decoded on the phone and are never stored or sent.

Nothing, unless you switch on Receive. Then it writes the measurements your own Home Assistant sends into Health Connect: weight, height, body fat, lean body mass, bone mass, body water mass and blood pressure, each behind its own switch and its own permission. It can only change records it wrote itself.

Only to the destinations you enter: your own webhook URLs and your own MQTT broker. The app contacts no other server. There are no analytics, no crash reporting services and no advertising SDKs. Besides the types you switch on, each payload carries the app version, and a Screen Time payload also the phone\'s manufacturer and model. Every Health Connect record carries its ID in Health Connect (uuid) and the package name of the app that wrote it (source), which tells your server which apps you use. With Record metadata in payload on (off by default), each record also carries when it was last changed, the writing app\'s own ID and version for it, how it was recorded, the device\'s manufacturer, model and type, and the time zone offset. MQTT is unencrypted unless you switch on TLS. States are published retained, so the broker keeps the latest value of each sensor, for Screen Time also the most used apps, even after you switch MQTT off in the app: clear the topics on the broker if you stop using it.

Your settings, with secrets in encrypted storage that is left out of cloud backup. Sync progress, so each record is sent once. A log of the last 100 deliveries, which you can clear, and payloads that could not be delivered yet. Uninstalling the app removes all of it. Exports are files you create yourself: the app keeps a copy in its cache until your next export, or until it starts a day later, and hands it to the share sheet, where the app you pick keeps its own copy. A settings export without secrets still contains your webhook URLs, which can work as a password, so share it with care.
Everything is opt-in and reversible: which types are read, where they go, how often, and what is written. Revoking a permission in Android stops the matching reads and writes immediately.
Questions about privacy: open an issue on GitHub or email the developer at the address on the GitHub profile.
